title: GND check/validate/verify JSON payload (D-10, D-11, D-12)
description: Draft 2020-12 schema for the `--format json` payload emitted by `python -m gnd check`, `python -m gnd validate`, and `python -m gnd verify`. This is a runtime OUTPUT contract, not an interchange format — it is deliberately vendored-only and lives outside src/gnd/schema/, which tests/test_schema_sync.py holds byte-identical to the gnd-orm-core canonical references. One of two closed fixed-shape tagged records is emitted on every exit path that carries a verdict (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 70); exit 64 (argparse usage error) deliberately emits none. Version 3 preserves the original keys and forbids `derivations`; version 4 requires it. Within either variant every key is always present with an empty default, and `outcome` is the exit discriminator. Bump `schema_version` on any breaking change.

source.description: The constraint's declared provenance origin (R-01), read from the constraint itself: explicit | sample | common-sense | llm-inferred | user-supplied | imported (v2). PANEL-3 scoping: only source + status are surfaced; the full provenance block (user_quote etc.) is deliberately NOT copied into reports — additionalProperties:false enforces the exclusion.

status.description: The constraint's confirmation status (R-01): proposed | confirmed. The only other provenance field PANEL-3 admits into the payload.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable reason a constraint could not be evaluated (D-12). Non-null if and only if verdict is 'unchecked'.

extraction.description: The extractor half of `gnd verify` (R-03''/PANEL-3): its fidelity record, kept SEPARATE from the checker's verdicts so the full verifier's two error sources are never blended. Present as {} on every `check`/`validate` payload — populated only by `gnd verify` (whose builder and tests enforce populated-ness on that path); deliberately NO required list here so the empty object validates.

state.description: R-13': the extraction-state vocabulary. `skipped` is written ONLY by an intentional opt-out; absence of files is `failed`, never `skipped`.

sidecar.description: The sidecar path as given on the command line.

schema_version.description: Four closed variants, paired by derivation class and by whether the payload names the model that produced it. 3 is the frozen non-structured payload and 4 the frozen structured one; both forbid `model_digest` and remain exactly what they were. 5 and 6 are their model-bound successors, selected by `gnd check` and `gnd verify` once a model has loaded, and both require `model_digest`. A single new version cannot carry both fixed shapes, so the discriminator that already separates 3 from 4 separates 5 from 6 (v5.1 Phase 3, D-P3.1). Version 7 adds a fixed assurance union; versions 3-6 remain frozen.

anyOf.description: The identity of the model this payload was produced from, as `gnd.transition.model_digest` computes it -- the same function a population's validation marker and a walk's `steps.json` use, so a report, a population and a walk agree by construction about what 'this model' means. Present on versions 5 and 6 and forbidden on 3 and 4. A model PATH is a coordinate, not an identity: two models can occupy one path over time and one model can be read from two. Emitted immediately after `model` so the byte delta from the frozen variants is exactly two keys wide.

transition.description: The walk, when one was run. THREE-VALUED BY DESIGN, and the distinction is why this key is always present: `null` means this invocation was not a transition run at all; an object with `evaluated: false` means a walk was REFUSED before evaluation began, with the rejection itself travelling in `issues` under a transition:* rule id; `evaluated: true` means a walk was evaluated and the report members are populated. A consumer therefore never has to read `exit_code` to tell 'not a walk' from 'a walk we would not run'.

evaluated.description: Whether the walk was evaluated. False means gnd.transition refused it -- exit 3, before any state was computed.

model_digest.description: As SUPPLIED by the steps document, not as computed here: when a run is refused for a digest mismatch, the caller needs to see what they sent. Null when the document could not be parsed far enough to carry one.

pre_snapshot_verdicts.description: Null when the walk was refused before evaluation -- 'we did not look', which an empty array would misreport as 'we looked and found none'.

items.description: One finding about the walk. Two invariants the model enforces are restated here so a consumer reading only the schema learns them: `reason_code` is non-null if and only if `verdict` is 'unchecked', and `direction` is non-null if and only if `family` is 'frame'.

steps.description: Null when the walk was refused before evaluation -- 'we did not look', which an empty array would misreport as 'we looked and found none'.

frame_verdicts.description: Null when the walk was refused before evaluation -- 'we did not look', which an empty array would misreport as 'we looked and found none'.

exit_code.description: The process exit code. Band precedence is 3 > 1 > 4 > 2 > 0 (D-08).

acceptance_ready.description: True if and only if exit_code is 0 (D-08). 'Could not decide' (4) is never acceptance.

model.description: Path to the model as supplied on the command line.

population.description: Path to the population; always null for command 'validate'.

counts.description: Verdict tally, passed through unchanged from CheckReport.counts() — the same dict the text renderer prints, so the two renderings can never disagree.

verdicts.description: One entry per constraint. Empty on exit 3 and 70 (the checker never ran) and for command 'validate'.

anyOf.description: One alethic obligation per derived fact type; present only in schema version 4.

coverage.description: Declared-coverage status and fact count per fact type.

issues.description: Error-severity validation issues, populated on exit 3. Capped at MAX_POPULATION_ISSUES (200) so an untrusted population cannot produce an unbounded payload (T-01.1-02).

issues_total.description: Issue count BEFORE truncation. Equals len(issues) unless issues_truncated is true.

issues_truncated.description: True when issues_total exceeded the cap and the array was elided.

warnings.description: Warning-severity issues (e.g. semantic:modality-policy). Never block a load.

error.description: Populated on exit 70 (internal checker error) and on the opaque exit-3 load-failure arm where no structured issues exist. Null otherwise.
